title: Decoder hypothesis rack: model affinity, soft-retracts, and acceptance telemetry
creator: Lina Chen
description: Proposal and implementation plan for a lightweight runtime construct we call the 'hypothesis rack' to support speculative decoding: it manages model affinity scoring (kernel/hardware-aware), issues prefill probes, records acceptance signals, and performs soft-retract fallbacks. Goal: enable lower-latency speculative outputs while bounding cost and maintaining deterministic fallbacks for failing acceptance conditions.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Runtime can schedule a speculative prefill probe to a candidate model and record an acceptance score within 30ms of probe completion.
2) If acceptance score >= threshold, switch to candidate decoder and stream speculative tokens; else fallback to baseline model without visible duplication to caller.
3) Telemetry emits per-request candidate scores, kernel affinity tag, probe latency, and final decision.
4) End-to-end p95 latency improvement of >=8% for targeted workloads in lab harness without >1% increase in token cost.
5) Feature gate and rollout plan exist for canary and gradual ramp to 20% traffic with automatic rollback on regression alerts.
design_notes: Hypothesis rack sits between request admission and decode scheduler. Key components: affinity scorer (model+kernel fingerprint -> score), probe dispatcher (prefill micro-batch with short token budget), acceptance evaluator (confidence metric based on top-k token overlap + soft alignment), and retract controller (graceful handoff preserving token order). We prefer lightweight probes (<=8 tokens) to minimize cost. Kernel selection heuristics use precomputed fingerprints and recent latency samples. See design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SERV/Decoder+Hypothesis+Rack+Design
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Probe cost vs. latency: larger probes increase accuracy of acceptance but raise token cost. We choose 6-8 token probes as a compromise.
- Kernel affinity staleness: hardware changes or quantization profiles may invalidate fingerprints; mitigation: continuous fingerprint reconciler job and decayed scores.
- Ordering complexity: speculative tokens must be retractable without confusing callers; implement soft-retracts that emit a short "edit boundary" event in streaming protocol.
- Failure modes: network loss during handoff could cause duplicate responses; mitigate with idempotent commit markers and short-lived lease for speculative assignments.
implementation_plan:
1) Prototype affinity scorer and probe dispatcher in runtime feature branch (2 weeks).
2) Add acceptance evaluator and acceptance telemetry hooks (1 week).
3) Implement retract controller and streaming protocol markers (2 weeks).
4) Lab harness synthetic experiments + model zoo run (1 week).
5) Canary rollout behind feature flag with 5% -> 20% ramp and automated regression checks (2 weeks).
tasks: ENG-100502 implement affinity scorer and fingerprint table
ENG-100503 probe dispatcher + short prefill micro-batch
ENG-100505 retract controller + streaming edit boundary
telemetry_and_metrics: Emit: candidate_accept_score, probe_tokens, probe_latency_ms, kernel_affinity_id, handoff_latency_ms, final_model_id, speculative_commit_flag. Dashboards: spec_decode_overview (p50/p95 latency by decision path), spec_cost_delta, rollback_rate. Alerts: rollback_rate > 0.5% or spec_cost_delta > 3% over baseline.
qa_plan: Unit tests for scorer, integration tests for probe->evaluate->commit flow with simulated failures, fuzz tests for streaming retract sequences. Load test against lab harness with mixtures of short-chat, long-form, and code generation prompts. Compare output quality via eval set and compute model-output divergence with and without speculation.
rollout_and_rollback: Feature-flagged gate. Rollout sequence: internal-only -> devorg -> 5% canary -> 20% ramp. Automatic rollback triggers: regression alerts from telemetry, customer error rate increase, or >2s regressions in p99 latency. Manual kill switch in runtime console for immediate fallback to baseline routing.
